findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Only the verifier is warned that the repository's own tests fail in the hidden view; the producer, which can write, is not
findings.evidence: The study checks are cargo fmt, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` (athena.toml:114-125), and the producer's grant includes test and clippy (athena.toml:107). ProducerInputs.checks (crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs:357) lists the checks to the producer. In a Hermes job's hidden snapshot, the athena-cli test module embeds studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json at compile time (drain.rs:5017, inside #[cfg(test)] starting at :4682), so clippy --all-targets and cargo test fail to compile. The cap-study rules tests panic (rules.rs:1435), and so does the new criterion-1 test. Study admission only refuses build output (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:112-124), so a producer that edits those tests to 'fix' them would have the edits accepted and landed; only writes under hidden study directories are dropped. Decision 6 gives the verifier a code-built 'not a check' entry, but decision 8 gives the producer nothing except a design-doc note and a question to the user. Fix: When hidden_study_dirs(ctx) is non-empty, push a matching 'not a check', passed entry onto the producer's checks list in code. It should name the hidden directories and the tests that fail in this view (athena-cli drain tests, xtask site_page, cap-study rules, the criterion-1 test), say that the gate runs them on the full tree, and say they must not be edited to pass in this view. Assert the entry in the producer brief in the criterion-3 test, and its absence for the change job in 2(c). Optionally, also flag in the producer's `hidden` UI line any study-job edit to a file that reads a hidden study.

findings.summary: The reader's view is corrected by a second reader run, which depends on the reader's judgement, though an explicit system-naming form in the schema might make it unnecessary
findings.evidence: read_for (reading.rs:472-526) is extended so that a reading of a non-pinning capability made in the hidden view is discarded and the reader runs again on the full tree, with a new failure when the two runs disagree. The plan rejects keying on an explicit selector only because the selector's form could not be read in this copy (config.rs:413-416 has no systems map). Fix: In step 1, when the base's systems schema is read, check whether it has a dedicated way to name a system in the request (a field or fixed syntax, not a substring). If it does, decide the reader's view from that alone and keep the re-read only as the fallback. Say which was chosen in the final report.

findings.summary: The criterion-1 test reads firstmate's pin.json at run time, so it fails in a Hermes agent's hidden view and adds to the failing tests
findings.evidence: The plan reads ../../studies/firstmate-work-handling/pin.json at run time. In a Hermes producer's or verifier's snapshot that directory is hidden, so the test panics there. Decision 8 accepts this, but no message points the agent at the cause. Fix: Make the test's failure message say that the file is hidden from study agents and that the gate runs the test on the full tree, and include the test in the producer and verifier notes.

'the Tweak returns `study` on the hidden run only if the workdir lacks studies/a... precisely: first run (hidden) returns `change`, second (full tree) returns `study`' Fix: Keep only the final description: the first (hidden) run returns change, the second (full-tree) run returns study.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot code: snapshot.rs (create, materialize, change_list), pin.rs (pin_repo, study_pin), verification.rs (the Checked destructure, verifier_snapshot, reruns at :313/:341), reading.rs (read_for/read_once), run/mod.rs (where the pin is recorded, the checks and verify_dir), the three repo_url-stripping test helpers, every caller of Snapshot::create/materialize/change_list, and every reader of studies/ in the code. The dependents list matches what I found, and the design works on the code as it is. Specifically: the verifier rebuild at verify_dir is safe because verifier_snapshot removes the directory first; the pin is on the job record before the producer and verifier snapshots are made; and hidden directories land with their base bytes because they are absent from both sides of the snapshot diff. The systems schema is missing in this copy (config.rs has a single repo_url/repo_ref), and step 1 correctly stops instead of inventing it. One design gap is major. The plan warns only the verifier that the repository's own tests fail in a study job's hidden view. The producer is not warned, yet it has cargo test and clippy in its grant, sees the gate's checks listed in its brief, and its edits outside studies/ are not restricted by study admission. So an uninformed producer may "fix" the failing tests by editing them, and those edits would land. A code-built note in the producer's checks list, like the verifier entry, closes the gap. The remaining findings are minor or nits.
